Research Methods II · LE1

Multi-Year Repeat Index & Study Guide

Built from the uploaded 2025, 2026, and 2028 examinations. The emphasis is on what examiners repeatedly test, how the wording changes, and what every answer choice means. Historical answer keys are preserved even when the source itself contains a discrepancy.

3exam years analyzed
55PDF pages scanned
235questions extracted
43repeat families
182repeated question instances
16topic areas
Rationale standard: every choice is defined or explained as its own study point. The generated notes prioritize the exact exam rationale, clearer explanations from other exam years, then the project lectures. 53 questions appeared only once and are not mixed into the repeat-family interface.
Master RuleThe null hypothesis states no real difference or association. The alternative states that a difference or association exists. A directional/unidirectional alternative predicts which way the effect goes, while a bidirectional/two-tailed alternative predicts a difference without specifying direction.
Examiner PatternThe examiner repeatedly reverses “difference exists” vs “no difference,” then asks whether direction is stated.
Project-source basis: Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper

Q17
PDF page 3
Molnupiravir has no effect in development of COVID-19 severity. If this was a hypothesis of a research, what kind of hypothesis is the above statement?
A. Null hypothesis ✓
B. Negative hypothesis
C. Two-sided hypothesis
D. One-sided hypothesis
Original PDF rationale
Null hypothesis is always negative! No such thing as “negative hypothesis”
A
A.Null hypothesisKEYED ✓
Correct. A null hypothesis states that there is no real difference between groups or no real association between the independent and dependent variables.
B.Negative hypothesisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The project materials do not use 'negative hypothesis' as a formal type. A statement of no effect or no association is classified as the null hypothesis.
C.Two-sided hypothesisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A bidirectional or two-sided hypothesis states that a difference or association exists without predicting which direction it will take.
D.One-sided hypothesisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A unidirectional or one-sided alternative hypothesis predicts the direction of the relationship or difference, such as higher, lower, increased, or decreased.

Q23
PDF page 4
What describes the relationship between two or more variables allowing for the relationship to be tested empirically and summarizes the elements of the research study?
A. Hypothesis ✓
B. Objective
C. Strength of Association
D. Data Analysis
Original PDF rationale
Research hypothesis is a statement that describes the relationship between two or more variables allowing for the relationship to be tested empirically Objective - Aim or goal of the actions to be undertaken by the researcher Strength of Association - the degree to which the values of two variables vary or change together Data analysis - Estimates the effect of intervention/measures of treatment effect
A
A.HypothesisKEYED ✓
Correct. A research hypothesis is a testable prediction about the relationship between two or more variables and provides a basis for tests of statistical significance.
B.ObjectiveDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. An objective states what the researcher hopes to achieve. It guides data collection and analysis but is not itself the testable prediction of a relationship.
C.Strength of AssociationDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Strength of association describes how strongly variables vary together or how large an association is. It is a result or measure, not the prediction stated before analysis.
D.Data AnalysisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Data analysis is the process used to summarize and test collected data. It evaluates a hypothesis rather than serving as the hypothesis itself.

Q20
PDF page 5
Which of the following is a BIDIRECTIONAL HYPOTHESIS?
A. Medical students who learn online this semester have lower grades than those who learn in the physical classroom.
B. The grades of the first year medical students who learn online this semester are no different from those who learn in the physical classroom.
C. There is a significant difference in grades between medical students who learn online versus those who learn in the physical classroom this semester. ✓
D. None of the above
Original PDF rationale
Unidirectional Hypothesis ● states the direction of the relationship/difference between variables/groups ● Predicts one specific direction, like higher or lower. Bidirectional Hypothesis ● States only that there is a difference between variables/groups but does not say which is greater/smaller; ● Or states that there is an association between variables but does not say in which direction Reference trans/book: 📖 Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper (2028) and Citations, Use of AI
C
A.Medical students who learn online this semester have lower grades than those who learn in the physical classroom.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. This statement predicts a specific direction of difference, making it a unidirectional alternative hypothesis when used as a research hypothesis.
B.The grades of the first year medical students who learn online this semester are no different from those who learn in the physical classroom.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. This wording states no difference or no effect, which is the defining form of a null hypothesis.
C.There is a significant difference in grades between medical students who learn online versus those who learn in the physical classroom this semester.KEYED ✓
Correct. This states that a difference exists but does not specify which group is higher or lower, so it is a bidirectional alternative hypothesis.
D.None of the aboveDISTRACTOR

If the research investigators think that “adult urban settlers with monthly income less than PhP 10,000.00 are more likely to have storm anxiety” then formalize it as one of the STUDY HYPOTHESES, which of the following does it represent?

B. Null hypothesis, two-sided (Two-tailed)
C. Alternative hypothesis, one-sided (One-tailed) ✓

Original PDF rationale
● Null hypothesis (H₀) → Assumes no relationship between income level and storm anxiety. ● Alternative hypothesis (H₁) ○ Two-tailed: Would test for any difference (either higher or lower storm anxiety in low-income settlers). ○ One-tailed: Tests for a specific direction (e.g., low income → more storm anxiety). ● Since the researchers are explicitly predicting more storm anxiety in those earning < 10K, this is a directional hypothesis → Alternative hypothesis (One-tailed). Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper and Citations, Use of AI
C
A.Null hypothesisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A null hypothesis states that there is no real difference between groups or no real association between the independent and dependent variables.
B.Null hypothesis, two-sided (Two-tailed)DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A null hypothesis states that there is no real difference between groups or no real association between the independent and dependent variables.
C.Alternative hypothesis, one-sided (One-tailed)KEYED ✓
Correct. A unidirectional or one-sided alternative hypothesis predicts the direction of the relationship or difference, such as higher, lower, increased, or decreased.
D.Alternative hypothesis, two-sided (Two-tailed)DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A bidirectional or two-sided hypothesis states that a difference or association exists without predicting which direction it will take.
Master RuleA literature review critically summarizes and synthesizes existing research, identifies consensus, conflicts, and gaps, and supports the rationale for future research. It is not a mere list of summaries.
Examiner PatternThe examiner shifts from defining the review to asking why appraisal, systematic methods, and mastery of the field matter.

Q36
PDF page 5
A literature review may include which of the following:
A. All choices are correct ✓
B. A detailed review of existing literature on a particular topic of interest to the researcher
C. Current existing knowledge and the gaps in that knowledge
D. COnflicts and controversies
E. How your research proposal will address those gaps, conflicts, and controversies
Original PDF rationale
Based on RES 1.03 (2025) Definition of literature review: → Detailed review of existing research on a topic → Involves going through existing research ▪ Knowledge and findings ▪ Gaps or conflicts ▪ How your work addresses those gaps/conflicts → Basically answers why you are doing a particular research
A
A.All choices are correctKEYED ✓
Correct. The project source defines a literature review as a synthesis of existing research that identifies current knowledge, gaps, conflicts, and how the proposed work fits those gaps. Because the listed components all belong to that purpose, the combined choice is supported.
B.A detailed review of existing literature on a particular topic of interest to the researcherDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A literature review examines significant research related to the topic rather than merely listing sources. A detailed review of relevant literature is one component of that synthesis.
C.Current existing knowledge and the gaps in that knowledgeDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Identifying what is already known and where evidence is missing is a core purpose of the literature review.
D.COnflicts and controversiesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A literature review should identify contradictions, unresolved debates, and conflicts in the evidence rather than presenting only studies that agree.
E.How your research proposal will address those gaps, conflicts, and controversiesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A strong review shows how the proposed research responds to unresolved gaps, conflicts, or controversies in the existing evidence.
2026
Q33
PDF page 7
Which of the following statements best describes the LITERATURE REVIEW?
A. It is a list of all available literature on a research topic, with each source having a summary paragraph.
B. It is a critical assessment of existing references or previous studies that are found to be related to the research problem. ✓
C. It is a book review of all the sources a researcher has found related to his/her research problem.
D. It is a summary of all existing published articles that will directly support the hypothesis of the research study.
Original PDF rationale
LITERATURE REVIEW ● Available literature is read, reviewed and assessed to determine if there is already a solution to the problem. ● Not a book review and should only include a summary of the previous research related to the author's topic. ● Remember: Cite only major findings, ideas, generalizations, principles, or conclusions that are relevant to the present study.
B
A.It is a list of all available literature on a research topic, with each source having a summary paragraph.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A literature review is not a source-by-source list. It should synthesize major findings and connect them to the research question and knowledge gap.
B.It is a critical assessment of existing references or previous studies that are found to be related to the research problem.KEYED ✓
Correct. A literature review is a critical synthesis. It evaluates the relevance, rigor, bias risk, and applicability of studies rather than simply summarizing every source.
C.It is a book review of all the sources a researcher has found related to his/her research problem.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A medical literature review is not a book review. It critically synthesizes research evidence relevant to the problem.
D.It is a summary of all existing published articles that will directly support the hypothesis of the research study.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Selecting only studies that support the hypothesis would create a biased review. Relevant negative, null, and conflicting findings should also be considered.
2026
Q34
PDF page 8
Which of the following is TRUE about writing the REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE?
A. The researcher presents a critical evaluation of related studies and their appropriateness and applicability to the present study. ✓
B. Only non-print resources are acknowledged in the research proposal, as print sources are rarely used in the current setting.
C. The researcher must choose whether to use only local or foreign sources, but never both.
D. Each literature source is given a summarized paragraph with a comprehensive list of all the findings, principles, or conclusions found in that source.
Original PDF rationale
Acknowledge the resources (both print and electronic sources) you have referred to in your research proposal. Both can be used but divide the presentation into local and foreign sources. Cite only major findings, ideas, generalizations, principles, or conclusions that are relevant to the present study.
A
A.The researcher presents a critical evaluation of related studies and their appropriateness and applicability to the present study.KEYED ✓
Correct. A literature review is a critical synthesis. It evaluates the relevance, rigor, bias risk, and applicability of studies rather than simply summarizing every source.
B.Only non-print resources are acknowledged in the research proposal, as print sources are rarely used in the current setting.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Both print and electronic sources can be acknowledged. The important issue is relevance and credibility, not excluding an entire source format.
C.The researcher must choose whether to use only local or foreign sources, but never both.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Local and foreign literature can both be used when relevant. They may be organized separately, but the project source does not require choosing only one.
D.Each literature source is given a summarized paragraph with a comprehensive list of all the findings, principles, or conclusions found in that source.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The review should cite major relevant findings, ideas, principles, and conclusions rather than reproduce every finding from every source.

Q22
PDF page 6
Which of the following is a RIGOROUS, PROTOCOL-DRIVEN TYPE OF REVIEW?
A. Narrative Review
B. Systematic Review ✓
C. Editorial
D. Case Report
Original PDF rationale
Broad overview, no strict methodology Rigorous and protocol driven (primarily use PRISMA guidelines); follows strict methodologies to minimize bias Reported individually, without attempting to analyze or synthesize similarities across patients Reference trans/book: 📖 Review of Medical Literature, Electronic Search for Journals, Reference and Citations, Use of AI (2028)
B
A.Narrative ReviewDISTRACTOR

B.Systematic ReviewKEYED ✓

C.EditorialDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. An editorial is an opinion or commentary format rather than a protocol-driven synthesis of evidence.
D.Case ReportDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A case report describes an individual clinical case. It is not a review method and does not systematically synthesize multiple studies.

Q24
PDF page 6
What is a KEY PITFALL in LITERATURE REVIEWS?
A. citing too many references
B. including only high-impact journals
C. using only artificial tools (AI) tools for screening
D. ignoring negative or null results (i.e. selection bias) ✓
Original PDF rationale
Selection bias skews result by omitting studies that don’t support a hypothesis Reference trans/book: LE 1 Answer Key
D
A.citing too many referencesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The problem is not the raw number of references but whether they are relevant and critically synthesized. A well-focused review may cite many sources when warranted.
B.including only high-impact journalsDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. High-impact reputable journals are useful sources, but restricting the review only to them can miss relevant evidence. The core pitfall highlighted in the lecture is selective omission of studies.
C.using only artificial tools (AI) tools for screeningDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. AI tools can assist screening, but the project materials emphasize human oversight and critical appraisal. Using a tool does not remove the need to evaluate relevance, quality, and bias.
D.ignoring negative or null results (i.e. selection bias)KEYED ✓
Correct. Ignoring negative or null studies selectively favors one direction of evidence and creates selection bias in the review.

Q25
PDF page 6
Why is CRITICAL APPRAISAL important in LITERATURE REVIEWS?
A. To assess the validity and applicability of studies ✓
B. To reject all industry-funded studies
C. To shorten the review process
D. To avoid citing older papers
Original PDF rationale
Ensures evidence is reliable and relevant; critical appraisal evaluates study quality, bias, and relevance Reference trans/book: 📖 Review of Medical Literature, Electronic Search for Journals, Reference and Citations, Use of AI (2028)
A
A.To assess the validity and applicability of studiesKEYED ✓
Correct. Critical appraisal evaluates whether study findings are methodologically sound, at risk of bias, and applicable to the question being reviewed.
B.To reject all industry-funded studiesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Funding source can raise a conflict-of-interest concern, but critical appraisal evaluates each study’s methods and bias rather than automatically rejecting every industry-funded study.
C.To shorten the review processDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Critical appraisal is performed to judge evidence quality and relevance. Its purpose is not simply to shorten the review process.
D.To avoid citing older papersDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Older studies can still be appropriate when they establish historical foundations or the evolution of a concept. Critical appraisal focuses on quality and applicability, not age alone.

Master RuleCohort studies organize participants by exposure and follow them toward outcomes. Concurrent and non-concurrent cohorts preserve an exposure-to-outcome direction and commonly use relative risk/risk ratio.
Examiner PatternTime direction, follow-up, attrition, and risk-ratio interpretation are repeatedly used as cohort clues.

C. These studies may be purely descriptive in nature, and may include prevalence surveys to determine the public health burden of a specific medical condition.

Original PDF rationale
📖 2026 Trans 1.4 Review of Research Designs: Qualitative Research VS Quantitative Research Cross-Sectional Study ● Advantages: ○ A major strength of cross-sectional studies over cohort studies and clinical trials is that there is no waiting for the outcome to occur. ○ This makes them fast and inexpensive, and it means that there is no loss to follow-up. ● Disadvantages: ○ A weakness of cross-sectional studies is the difficulty of establishing causal relationships from observational data collected in a cross-sectional time frame. ○ Cross-sectional studies are also impractical for the study of rare diseases if the design involves collecting data on a sample of individuals from the general population.
A
A.These studies are prone to systematic errors, including possible high attrition rates or “lost to follow-up” issues.KEYED ✓
Correct. Loss to follow-up is mainly a concern in designs that track participants over time, especially cohorts. Cross-sectional studies have no prolonged follow-up period, so high attrition is not a defining feature.
B.These studies, if analytical in design, may not be able to establish temporality that will definitively establish causation.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. An analytical cross-sectional study measures exposure and outcome at the same time, so it may show association but cannot reliably establish which came first.
C.These studies may be purely descriptive in nature, and may include prevalence surveys to determine the public health burden of a specific medical condition.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Cross-sectional studies are commonly used as prevalence surveys because they measure the presence of a condition in a population at a defined point or short period.
D.These studies may be weakly analytical, wherein two variables (i.e., arbitrarily designated as “exposure” and “outcome”) are analyzed at a single point or period in time.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Measuring exposure and outcome at a single point or short period is the defining snapshot feature of cross-sectional research.

Which of the following best defines “CONFOUNDING” in MEDICAL RESEARCH?

B. A random error that decreases sample validity

D. A distortion of the exposure-outcome relationship by an extraneous factor ✓
Original PDF rationale
Information bias leads to to misclassification of subjects in one or more estimation of strength of association, variables and distortion of the estimate of effect Random error is a measurement error that fluctuates due to unpredictability or uncertainty inherent in the measuring process Systematic error or bias results from persisted issue, and it leads to a consistent error in measurement Confounding refers to a situation where an external factor (not a causal pathway) creates a false association between the exposure and outcome or masks a true association. Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) 05: Bias and Confounders
D
A.Inaccurate measurements of disease statusDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Inaccurate measurement of exposure or disease status is an information-bias problem. Confounding instead arises from an extraneous factor that distorts the exposure-outcome relationship.
B.A random error that decreases sample validityDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Random error is unpredictable variation between the observed and true value and can be reduced by increasing sample size. Confounding is a systematic distortion from a third factor.
C.A systematic error that pushed the actual results away from the truthDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Systematic error or bias is a consistent deviation from the truth in selection or information collection. Confounding is distinguished by distortion from an extraneous factor related to the study relationship.
D.A distortion of the exposure-outcome relationship by an extraneous factorKEYED ✓
Correct. This is the defining idea of confounding in the project material: an extraneous variable distorts the apparent relationship between exposure and outcome.

B. Age is only associated with physical activity
C. Age is only associated with myocardial infarction
D. Age is a risk factor for myocardial infarction and related to physical activity ✓
Original PDF rationale
A confounding variable is NOT part of an experiment, which adversely affects the relationship of the variables. Since both MI and PA are related to age as its risk factor, this could result in a masking of the true cause-and-effect relationship of the independent and dependent variable. ↑ age = ↑risk of MI and ↓PA Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) 05: Bias and Confounders
D
A.Age is caused by physical activityDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A confounder should not simply be a consequence of the exposure. This statement puts age downstream of physical activity, which does not fit the confounder relationship.
B.Age is only associated with physical activityDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Association with the exposure alone is insufficient for confounding. The third variable must also be related to the outcome.
C.Age is only associated with myocardial infarctionDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Association with the outcome alone is insufficient for confounding. The third variable must also be related to the exposure.
D.Age is a risk factor for myocardial infarction and related to physical activityKEYED ✓
Correct. For age to confound the physical-activity and myocardial-infarction relationship, it must be associated with the exposure and independently related to the outcome. This statement gives both conditions.

Incorrect. A lower allowed error means greater precision. Greater precision requires a larger sample, not a smaller one.

When your POPULATION IS SMALLER THAN THE DERIVED OR COMPUTED SAMPLE SIZE, which of the following is a reasonable step to take?

D. Employ the finite correction formula. ✓
Original PDF rationale
No original rationale was extracted for this item.
D
A.Get a larger populationDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Changing the population simply to fit a formula changes the research question. The finite population correction is the appropriate statistical adjustment when the actual population is small.
B.Change all your objectivesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Objectives should not be rewritten merely because the population is finite. The sample calculation can be adjusted with the finite population correction.
C.Change the population of interestDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Changing the population alters the intended generalization of the study. A finite population is handled statistically rather than by silently redefining the target.
D.Employ the finite correction formula.KEYED ✓
Correct. When the source population is small relative to the initially calculated sample, the finite population correction adjusts the required sample to account for sampling a substantial fraction of the population.

and those residing outside Payatas garbage dumpsite. D. These studies are helpful in generating hypotheses on possible cause-effect relationships.
Original PDF rationale
📖 2026 Trans 1.4 Review of Research Designs: Qualitative Research VS Quantitative Research Descriptive designs ● Observational studies which characterize the patterns of disease occurrence in relation to variables such as person, place, and time ● Whilst descriptive studies can highlight associations between variables or between exposure and outcome variables, they cannot establish causality. ● Hypothesis generation - can suggest hypotheses which can be tested in analytical observational studies.
A
A.These studies demonstrate temporality, which is essential in establishing causality of variables of interest.KEYED ✓
Correct. Descriptive studies generally characterize person, place, and time but do not establish exposure-before-outcome temporality required for causal inference. The statement therefore overstates what descriptive designs can establish.
B.These studies are generally observational designs, which characterize phenomena in terms of time, place, and person variables.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Descriptive studies are observational and characterize disease or phenomena by person, place, and time. This is a defining feature in the project lecture.
C.These studies may have limitations in terms of generalizability and/or external validity.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Descriptive reports, especially small case-based designs, can have limited generalizability because the observed group may not represent a wider population.
D.These studies are helpful in generating hypotheses on possible cause-effect relationships.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A central role of descriptive research is hypothesis generation. It describes patterns that can later be tested by analytical studies.
2028
Q94
PDF page 22
Which design GENERATES HYPOTHESES rather than TEST them?
A. Case report/series ✓
B. Quasi-experimental design
C. Randomized controlled trials
D. Cohort study
Original PDF rationale
A descriptive study, thus, hypothesis-generating All analytical studies, thus, test both null and alternative hypotheses. Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) 04 - Review of Research Designs
A
A.Case report/seriesKEYED ✓
Correct. A case report describes an individual patient or event and is mainly useful for generating hypotheses. Case reports and case series are classic descriptive designs used to generate hypotheses.
B.Quasi-experimental designDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. An experimental study includes an investigator-induced intervention. Randomized controlled trials are the strongest experimental design for testing causal hypotheses. Experimental and quasi-experimental designs test intervention effects rather than serving as simple descriptive reports.
C.Randomized controlled trialsDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A randomized controlled trial assigns interventions by randomization, which helps distribute potential confounders between groups and strengthens causal inference. Experimental and quasi-experimental designs test intervention effects rather than serving as simple descriptive reports.
D.Cohort studyDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A cohort study groups participants by exposure and follows the occurrence of outcomes. It can establish exposure before outcome and commonly uses relative risk. Cohort designs are analytical observational studies used for hypothesis testing rather than purely descriptive hypothesis generation.

Which of the following TERMINOLOGY-AND-DEFINITION matching is CORRECT?
A. Confounding variable : descriptive variable that has no effect on the study result
B. Background variable : has the potential to distort the study result
C. Independent variable : medical condition or disease state
D. Dependent variable: outcome of interest ✓
Original PDF rationale
Variable not included in the research but would have a probable impact on the outcome Demographic variable Variable that cause change outcome / effect of the independent variable Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper the tropical depression Crising and Habagat. D
A.Confounding variable : descriptive variable that has no effect on the study resultDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A confounding variable is an extraneous factor that can distort the relationship between the independent and dependent variables. It is not simply a harmless descriptive variable.
B.Background variable : has the potential to distort the study resultDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A background variable is a demographic or baseline characteristic such as age or sex that describes the study population. It is not defined as a variable that necessarily distorts the result.
C.Independent variable : medical condition or disease stateDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The independent variable is the exposure, input, or factor that may cause variation in the outcome. A disease state may be an outcome depending on the question, so disease is not the defining meaning of an independent variable.
D.Dependent variable: outcome of interestKEYED ✓
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome or effect that the study seeks to explain or measure. This directly matches the phrase 'outcome of interest.'

This topic specifically deals with how CCR5 expression is correlated to HIV transmission in comparison to individuals with decreased CCR5 gene expression. This is an example of a prevalence study.
A
A.Determining the relationship between a factor and an outcomeKEYED ✓
Correct. This wording directly tests whether CCR5 expression is associated with HIV transmission. It preserves the factor and outcome in the original problem without adding a different mechanism or population.

C.Identification of a possible cause of an eventDISTRACTOR

D.Testing the effectiveness of an intervention or programDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Effectiveness questions evaluate an intervention or program. CCR5 expression is being examined as a factor, not introduced as an intervention.

Which of the following statements best describes the “LIMIT” or “FILTER” function on MEDLINE / PubMed?
A. It refines the search yield by dictating specific characteristics of the target research papers (e.g., date of publication, study population, language used, etc.) ✓
B. It is also known as the medical sub-heading (MeSH), used for indexing articles for MEDLINE / PubMed.
C. They are operator terms which facilitate the searching of articles by grouping / including / excluding articles, depending on the operator term used.
D. It includes the use of quotation marks when searching for specific phrases on the search box
Original PDF rationale
2026 Trans 1.3 Review of Medical Literature & Electronic Search for Journals MeSH - provides a consistent way to retrieve information that may use different terminology of the same concept This describes BOOLEAN OPERATORS This is used in PHRASE SEARCHING
A
A.It refines the search yield by dictating specific characteristics of the target research papers (e.g., date of publication, study population, language used, etc.)KEYED ✓
Correct. Filters refine a search by limiting results to selected characteristics such as article type, publication date, language, or full-text availability.
B.It is also known as the medical sub-heading (MeSH), used for indexing articles for MEDLINE / PubMed.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. MeSH is a controlled vocabulary for subject indexing. It improves concept precision but is distinct from filters that limit by article characteristics.
C.They are operator terms which facilitate the searching of articles by grouping / including / excluding articles, depending on the operator term used.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Boolean operators combine or exclude search concepts. Filters instead limit the retrieved records by characteristics such as design, date, or language.
D.It includes the use of quotation marks when searching for specific phrases on the search boxDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Quotation marks are a phrase-searching technique. They are not the defining purpose of the filter function.

Which of the following represents the OVERALL, BROAD REACH of WHAT THE RESEARCH SEEKS OR EXPECTS TO ACHIEVE?
A. Research Problem
B. Research Hypothesis
C. General Objective ✓
D. Significance of the Study
Original PDF rationale
🗣️The Research Problem forms the basis that propels the inquiry, from which the Research Question is often derived. 🗣️Overall purpose of the research and represents what the research wants to do on a whole. 🗣️The Significance represents the higher reaching of the research and the value of study results in the larger context. Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper
C
A.Research ProblemDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The research problem is the question or issue the study is designed to answer. The general objective is usually the declarative statement of what the researcher plans to achieve in response to that problem.
B.Research HypothesisDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A research hypothesis predicts a relationship or difference between variables and provides the basis for statistical testing. It is not the overall action statement that directly restates what the study will accomplish.
C.General ObjectiveKEYED ✓
Correct. The general objective states the overall outcome the research expects to achieve and is derived directly from the research problem. It is often a declarative version of the research question.
D.Significance of the StudyDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Significance explains why the research matters and how it may add to knowledge or practice. It does not state the study’s overall task in the way the general objective does.

Which of the following is the BEST choice for GENERAL OBJECTIVE for the study?
A. To determine the awareness and knowledge of adult urban settlers in Metro Manila about storm anxiety ✓
B. To determine the proportion of adult urban settlers in Metro Manila who have storm anxiety
C. To determine the mean age of adult urban settlers who have storm anxiety
D. To develop a standardized, validated tool to measure storm anxiety
Original PDF rationale
General Objective - States what is expected to be achieved or the outcomes of the research in over-all terms Specific Objective ● Systematically addresses various parts of the research problem ○ How to achieve main goals step-by-step ● Break down a general objective into SMALLER, LOGICALLY CONNECTED parts. Reference trans/book: 📖 (2028) Writing the Introduction for a Research Paper
A
A.To determine the awareness and knowledge of adult urban settlers in Metro Manila about storm anxietyKEYED ✓
Correct. This objective measures awareness and knowledge, which are additional variables. It is appropriate only if those variables are part of the stated general objective and required to answer it.
B.To determine the proportion of adult urban settlers in Metro Manila who have storm anxietyDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Determining the proportion of the target population with storm anxiety is a measurable quantitative objective that directly describes the magnitude of the stated outcome.
C.To determine the mean age of adult urban settlers who have storm anxietyDISTRACTOR

D.To develop a standardized, validated tool to measure storm anxietyDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Developing and validating a measurement tool is a separate methodological objective. It would be appropriate only if instrument development were part of the research problem.

One pharmaceutical company is looking into the EFFICACY of a NEW MOLECULE (e.g.,Balcinrenone) versus the CURRENT NON-STEROIDAL MINERALOCORTICOID ANTAGONISTS (e.g., Spironolactone or Finerenone), as part of the medical management of adult patients with high failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In NEW DRUG DEVELOPMENT TRIALS, this represents which PHASE?
A. Phase I
B. Phase II
C. Phase III ✓
D. Phase IV
Original PDF rationale
Phase 1: Safety ● Healthy volunteers ● Sample size: 20 to 80 ● Single, unblinded, uncontrolled ● Determination of metabolic and pharmacologic actions, and the maximally tolerated dose Phase 2: Efficacy ● Individuals with target disease ● Sample size 100 to 300 ● Pracebo-controlled comparisons ● Evaluation of effectiveness, determination of short-term side effects and identification of common risks Phase 3: Preparatory ● Individuals with target disease ● Sample size: hundreds to thousands ● Randomized, controlled with 2 to 3 treatment arms ● Obtain additional information about effectiveness and evaluation of overall risk-benefit ratio ● Determination whether the new treatment is better than the standard treatment Phase 4: Understanding ● Individuals with target disease and new age groups, gender, etc. ● Sample size: thousands ● Uncontrolled, observational ● Monitoring of ongoing safety in large populations and identification of additional uses of the agent Reference trans/book: Epidemiology
C
A.Phase IDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Phase I is the first human testing stage and focuses primarily on safety, pharmacology, and toxicity, usually in a small group.
B.Phase IIDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Phase II studies whether the new treatment works while continuing safety evaluation, commonly in roughly 100 to 300 participants in the project source.
C.Phase IIIKEYED ✓
Correct. Phase III uses larger randomized comparative trials to determine how the new treatment performs against standard treatment and to further establish efficacy and safety.
D.Phase IVDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Phase IV occurs after marketing and gathers additional information on real-world use, effectiveness, and adverse effects.

A multi-center real world evidence study was conducted to determine the cardiorenal safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists in the management of hyperglycemia in the primary care setting. Investigators identified adult diabetics consulting at selected Family and Community Medicine out-patient clinics in the National Capital Region. The investigators identified diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and recruited study subjects with a 1:1 ratio. They also included patients with chronic kidney disease (Stages 1 and 2 vs. Stages 3 and 4) but excluded those with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) or Stage 5 CKD on hemodialysis and those who have undergone kidney transplantation. What type of PROBABILITY SAMPLING was employed?
A. Stratified Random Sampling ✓
B. Multi-Stage Random Sampling
C. Quota Sampling
D. Systematic Sampling
Original PDF rationale
A. Stratified Random Sampling - The population is first divided into non-overlapping groups called strata, then simple random sample is then selected from each stratum B. Multi- Stage Random Sampling- Complete sampling frame is necessary only for the primary sampling units, while the sampling frames for secondary/ succeeding stages of selection are only confined to those selected as samples C. Quota Sampling - non-probablility sampling method. D. Systematic Sampling - Variation of simple random sampling. This may be used when the sampling united are too numerous to number for purposes of simple random sampling. May also be used when a frame is not available. The sampling interval is “k” first determined where “k”is the ratio of the population size which is denoted by the capital letter “N” to the sample size, which is represented by the small case “n” leading to the formula: → k = N/n = 80/10 = 8
A
A.Stratified Random SamplingKEYED ✓
Correct. Stratified random sampling divides the population into meaningful strata and randomly samples within each stratum so important subgroups are represented.
B.Multi-Stage Random SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Multi-stage sampling performs selection in successive stages, such as choosing regions, then facilities, then individuals. It is broader than simply using a fixed systematic interval.
C.Quota SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Quota sampling fills predetermined subgroup numbers without random selection and is therefore a non-probability method.
D.Systematic SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Systematic sampling begins with a random start and then selects every kth unit according to a calculated sampling interval.

Q75
PDF page 20
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
A. Cluster sampling is a form of non-probability sampling where groups of individuals are chosen at will.
B. Multi-stage sampling is like a complex form of systematic sampling.
C. The terms “random selection” and “randomization” are synonymous and equivalent.
D. Systematic sampling utilizes a sampling interval after starting off randomly. ✓
Original PDF rationale
It is a form of PROBABILITY SAMPLING ● Simple Random Sampling = Raffle draw ● Systematic Sampling = Starts random but employs sampling interval after ● Stratified Sampling = Stratification into homogeneous groups →Selection per group ● Cluster Sampling = Selection of the entire cluster/group ● Multi-stage group = Clusters of the selected people are split into sub-groups to make it simpler for primary data collection It is a form of cluster sampling Random selection ≠Randomization ● Randomization – assignment by chance to one of two or more intervention groups ● Random selection – every member has the same chance as any other Random →Employs sampling interval
D
A.Cluster sampling is a form of non-probability sampling where groups of individuals are chosen at will.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Cluster sampling is a probability method that selects naturally occurring groups or clusters by a chance procedure. Choosing groups 'at will' would not be true cluster probability sampling.
B.Multi-stage sampling is like a complex form of systematic sampling.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Multi-stage sampling performs selection in successive stages, such as choosing regions, then facilities, then individuals. It is broader than simply using a fixed systematic interval.
C.The terms “random selection” and “randomization” are synonymous and equivalent.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Random selection chooses who enters the sample, while randomization assigns enrolled participants to study groups. They are related chance procedures but are not synonymous.
D.Systematic sampling utilizes a sampling interval after starting off randomly.KEYED ✓
Correct. Systematic sampling begins with a random start and then selects every kth unit according to a calculated sampling interval.

A.Does everybody get an equal chance to be selected?KEYED ✓

B.How will the people be chosen?DISTRACTOR

Q16
PDF page 3
Which of the following is a characteristic of an objective of a second year medical student in Research Methods 2?
A. Specific - should state what you are really trying to measure ✓
B. Time bound - this should be dynamic to satisfy objectives
C. Relationship - should investigate association of variables
D. Memorable - describes the current situation of variable
Original PDF rationale
Attainable/Achievable ▪ “Can the person do it?” ▪ “Can the measurable objective be achieved by the person? ▪ Does the research investigator/s have the experience, knowledge, or capability of fulfilling the expectation?” ▪ “Can it be done given the time frame, opportunity, and resources?” Relevant ▪ “Should it be done, and if so, why?” ▪ “What will be the potential impact of the study results?” ▪ “Is the objective of the research aligned with the research agenda of the investigators?” Timebound “When will it be done?”
A
A.Specific - should state what you are really trying to measureKEYED ✓
Correct. Specific means the objective clearly states what the study is trying to solve or measure, including the relevant variables and, when appropriate, the measurement instrument.
B.Time bound - this should be dynamic to satisfy objectivesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Time-bound means the objective specifies when the study or endpoint will occur, such as a school year or defined months of implementation.
C.Relationship - should investigate association of variablesDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Relationship is not one of the SMART components. An objective may examine an association, but SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable or Attainable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
D.Memorable - describes the current situation of variableDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Memorable is not a SMART criterion. The framework uses Measurable for M.

B. relevant

Original PDF rationale
While the stem of the question mentions a time element, this is not what is meant by "Timebound" and so Choice A is wrong. The statement doesn’t mention a timeframe (e.g., “within one semester” or “in the past month”). While eventually the answer may have relevance and significance on a larger scale, these are not the best answers. It may be relevant, but the phrasing doesn’t emphasize relevance to a broader issue. The mention of "mean length of time (reported in hours)" shows measurability, and hence Choice C is the correct answer. It is somewhat specific (medical students, sleep duration), but the main highlighted characteristic is that it is measurable. The following are TRUE about a GOOD SAMPLE of study participants, EXCEPT:

Criteria for a good sampling design: ● The sample should be a representative of the population ● Sample should reflect both the characteristics and variability of the population ● Sample size should be adequate ● Practicality and feasibility of the sampling procedures must be simple and straightforward ● Economy and efficiency of the sampling design will ensure hughes level of information to be obtained at smallest cost

A.It is large enough to allow valid generalization of the study.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A good sample has adequate size to support valid analysis and reasonable generalization, while still being feasible.
B.It can be studied within reasonable expense and time requirements.DISTRACTOR

D.study participants / patientsDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Participant blinding means patients do not know which intervention they receive and is the basic layer present in single, double, and triple blinding.

The participant is the only one blinded. Both the participants and the investigators, the ones giving the intervention and evaluating outcomes, are blinded. A.It is the US National Library of Medicine’s controlled vocabulary used for indexing articles for MEDLINE, as a consistent way to retrieve information that may use different terminology for the same concept.KEYED ✓

B.They are operator terms which facilitate the searching of articles by grouping / including / excluding articles, depending on the operator term used.DISTRACTOR

Q55

A group of Filipino businessmen wanted to start a food-truck business in New York City, which will offer the Filipino favorite red jumbo hotdogs with red banana ketchup – a favorite dish among Filipinos but not known to many Americans. They did a preliminary feasibility study by randomly asking American passengers at the Grand Central Terminal for a free food taste and to answer a simple survey regarding the Filipino favorite snack. What type of NON-PROBABILITY SAMPLING has been employed?
A. Haphazard Sampling ✓
B. Quota Sampling
C. Judgemental Sampling
D. Simple Random Sampling
Original PDF rationale
May be likened to convenience sampling, where a researcher may sometimes use in their study whatever items come at hand or whomever is available. Researcher assistants may be given instructions to keep on interviewing household heads in a given place until the pre-specified quota for that accessible area has been reached. Most commonly employed type of non-probability sampling. A “representative” sample of the population is selected based on an expert’s subjective judgment or on some pre-specified criteria. A type of probability sampling. The most basic probability sampling. Its main characteristic is that every element in the population has an equal chance of being included in the sample.
A
A.Haphazard SamplingKEYED ✓
Correct. Haphazard or convenience sampling recruits readily available people without a probability mechanism. It is easy to conduct but may not represent the target population.
B.Quota SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Quota sampling is a non-probability method that fills preset numbers within selected categories without random selection within those categories.
C.Judgemental SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Judgmental or purposive sampling deliberately chooses participants because they possess characteristics considered important to the research question.
D.Simple Random SamplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Simple random sampling is a probability technique in which eligible members of the sampling frame are selected by chance.

NON-PROBABILITY SAMPLING: ● Convenience – recruits anyone who is available ● Consecutive – Participants enter the study one after the other; BEST non-prob sampling ● Quota Sampling – Data collectors are often given quotas ● Purposive – sample thought to be “representative” of the population is selected based on an expert’s subjective judgment ● Snowball / Chain referral – First used in research with “hidden populations” as the target study participants

B.Quota samplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Quota sampling is a non-probability method that fills preset numbers within selected categories without random selection within those categories.
C.Convenience samplingDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Haphazard or convenience sampling recruits readily available people without a probability mechanism. It is easy to conduct but may not represent the target population.
D.Consecutive samplingKEYED ✓
Correct. Consecutive sampling includes every eligible subject who appears during a defined recruitment period until the required sample is reached. Among non-probability methods it reduces arbitrary cherry-picking compared with convenience sampling.

Q57
PDF page 9
Which of the following statements on the NON-RESPONSE RATE is TRUE?
A. The proportion of subjects selected for the study who consent to be enrolled influences the validity of inferring that the enrolled sample represents the population. ✓
B. The level of non-response can potentially compromise the internal validity of the study.
C. A significant non-response rate does not distort the estimate of the prevalence of a chronic non-communicable disease.
D. An acceptable non-response rate may be set at 50% or below for most cross-sectional studies.
Original PDF rationale
If the non-response is only related to the exposure and not to the disease, this affects the distribution of the exposure in the study but not the observed effect, e.g. the relative risk, and thus it does not affect the internal validity of the study. It does distort the estimate of the prevalence as nonresponse bias may occur. Total nonresponse should not exceed 30 percent for any analyzed variable. Hypothesis testing for the difference between population means to compare or determine if there is a significant difference in the mean blood
A
A.The proportion of subjects selected for the study who consent to be enrolled influences the validity of inferring that the enrolled sample represents the population.KEYED ✓
Correct. Response rate affects how well the enrolled sample represents the intended population. If responders differ systematically from non-responders, estimates may be biased.
B.The level of non-response can potentially compromise the internal validity of the study.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Non-response can create selection bias when those who participate differ from those who do not. The project notes that distortion depends on how non-response relates to the exposure and outcome, so its effect is not automatic in every study.
C.A significant non-response rate does not distort the estimate of the prevalence of a chronic non-communicable disease.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. A substantial non-response rate can distort prevalence estimates if respondents differ from non-respondents on the condition or related factors.
D.An acceptable non-response rate may be set at 50% or below for most cross-sectional studies.DISTRACTOR
Incorrect. The project material recommends keeping non-response substantially lower than this. A very high non-response rate threatens representativeness.
2028
Q56
PDF page 14
Researchers wanted to know how computer scientists perceived a NEW SOFTWARE PROGRAM. When they distributed the survey forms, they found that many computer scientists either did not respond at all or initially responded but eventually quit before completing the entire survey. When researchers got the data back, they learned that the respondents perceived the software to be excellent and of high quality. However, once they rolled out the new software to the entire population of computer scientists, they realized that they received mostly negative feedback. This illustrates what TYPE OF BIAS?
A. Hawthorne bias
B. Prevarication bias
C. Loss to follow up bias
D. Non-response bias ✓
Original PDF rationale
[Under prevarication bias] Also known as the observer effect. People’s tendency to behave differently when they become aware that they are being observed. A subject may consciously feel the need to provide answers pleasing the interviewer or study coordinator. If the individual lost to follow up differs with respect to the exposure and outcome from those who remain in the study. It turns out that the people who took the time to complete the entire survey turned out to be mostly entry-level computer scientists who were unable to assess the flaws of the program. Due to this, respondents of the survey did not reflect the larger computer scientist population as whole and thus the results were unreliable. Reference trans/book: 📖 05 - Bias and Confounders
D
A.Hawthorne biasDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Hawthorne bias occurs when participants alter behavior because they know they are being observed. It is not the missing-participation problem described in the stem.
B.Prevarication biasDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Prevarication bias occurs when participants consciously misreport or deceive. Non-response instead occurs when selected people do not participate or fail to provide data.
C.Loss to follow up biasDISTRACTOR
Incorrect. Loss to follow-up occurs after participants have entered a longitudinal study and later drop out. Non-response occurs at recruitment or survey response when selected individuals do not respond.
D.Non-response biasKEYED ✓
Correct. Non-response bias occurs when selected individuals do not respond and the responders differ meaningfully from non-responders, making the observed sample unrepresentative.

Those identified by the index study subject will be the next respondents and the process continues until the desired sample size has been reached. Non-Probability Sampling ● Aka: Non-random sampling ● Main Characteristic: Chances of each member of the population to be selected in the sample will be difficult to determine or cannot be easily specified ● No way of assessing the reliability of the sample results ● Standard errors can’t be computed and and methods of statistical inference cannot be applied ● Best utilizied for descriptive purposes, rather than for making generalization or inferences about the target population B. Convenience Sampling - likened to accidental or haphazard sampling. “Whoever is available and willing gets automatically recruited” D.
